title: Recover the right note and prove intended-user access
goal: Resolve a misleading recovery handover where both backups are valid and privileged reading hides a restored-file access fault.
challenge: Use independent expected contents to select between two valid compressed notes. Restore separately, reject the older payload, retain failed learner-read evidence and repair only the restored copy. Verify actual learner access, contents and originals. Explain what the evidence does not establish.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/operations-handover.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/operations-handover.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; dir_ok() { test -d "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(realpath -e -- "$1")" = "$w/$1"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here && test "$(df --output=avail -k . | tail -1)" -gt 65536
steps.explanation: Create and record a new private guest workspace. Stop on any failed guard; the free-space check is an observation, not a guaranteed reserve. Do not use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A unique learner-owned mode0700 directory; no originals overwritten.

steps.command: here && fresh original.txt old.txt expected.sha old.gz good.gz archive.sha restored.txt denied.txt && printf 'CHANGE-42 approved\n' > original.txt && printf 'CHANGE-41 superseded\n' > old.txt && sha256sum original.txt > expected.sha && gzip -n -c original.txt > good.gz && gzip -n -c old.txt > old.gz && sha256sum good.gz old.gz > archive.sha && gzip -t good.gz old.gz
steps.explanation: Both known fixture streams are valid; format checks do not establish the correct recovery point. Preserve all originals and hashes.
steps.expected: Two backups, independent source expectation; no extraction over live files.

steps.command: here && fresh restored.txt denied.txt && { gzip -dc old.gz | cmp -s - original.txt; ps=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}"); test "${ps[*]}" = '0 1'; } && gzip -dc good.gz > restored.txt && cmp original.txt restored.txt && chmod 0000 restored.txt && sudo cat restored.txt && { cat restored.txt > denied.txt 2>&1; rc=$?; test "$rc" != 0; } && grep -qi 'permission denied' denied.txt
steps.explanation: Root can read a mode0000 file: that is not intended-user access. The wrong backup is valid but demonstrably not the expected payload.
steps.expected: Wrong payload refused; root read succeeds while the actual learner read fails.

steps.command: here && test -f restored.txt && test ! -L restored.txt && test "$(stat -c %U restored.txt)" = learner && chmod 0600 restored.txt && test "$(stat -c %U:%a restored.txt)" = learner:600 && cat restored.txt && cmp original.txt restored.txt && sha256sum -c expected.sha archive.sha
steps.explanation: Repair only this learner-owned restored copy, not the source or account policy. Independently explain payload selection, access evidence, uncertainty and next checks.
steps.expected: Actual learner read succeeds with expected contents; originals and both backups unchanged.

hints: A valid compressed stream may contain the wrong version.
Verify as the intended identity; root reading is not enough.
review: I retained actual statuses, bytes and relevant identities, including the incorrect case; successful command exit alone is not my evidence.
I can explain the stated limitations and independently meet the Challenge outcomes. Completion records my self-review, not an automatic assessment.
I preserved originals and inspected the exact cleanup inventory before deleting only this recorded practice workspace.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0:104.5 access reinforcement. LPIC-2 v4.5.0:206.2 recovery reinforcement. Self-reviewed and unscored; no full coverage.
